title: Microsoft Teams: third-party synthetic audio and video detection in meetings
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout facts, opt-in configuration, provider licensing and controls are supported. One minor clarification should flag Microsoft's conflicting descriptions of the provider identifier; the briefing correctly follows the cmdlet reference.

claims.claim: This Teams change introduces third-party synthetic audio and video detection in meetings.
claims.quote: Organizations can enhance meeting security with synthetic audio and video detection solutions provided by certified third-party providers.

claims.claim: Third-party detection requires administrator opt-in, so it does not start if administrators configure no provider.
claims.quote: An admin allows the provider's Teams app and grants admin consent to the permissions it needs. The admin turns on synthetic audio and video detection in a Teams meeting policy, selects one provider, and assigns the policy to organizers.

claims.claim: A detection-specific Teams licence, price or meter is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams third party synthetic audio video detection meetings licensing license price meter provider fees'; opened feature prerequisites/FAQ, reportSyntheticMedia, Defender Teams support and provider listings. No detection-specific Teams licence, price or meter found.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams third party synthetic audio video detection meetings licensing license price meter provider fees'; opened feature Available detection providers and Reality Defender/Pindrop listings. They refer purchasing to providers and publish no provider fee.

claims.claim: The control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting protection > Synthetic audio and video detection provider > Turn on synthetic audio and video protection.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select an existing meeting policy ... Under Meeting protection, select a provider from the Synthetic audio and video detection provider dropdown list. The Turn on synthetic audio and video protection setting appears

claims.where: controls[0].api; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy-name> -SyntheticMediaDetection Enabled -SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId <supported-provider-app-id> permits detection with the provider's Teams App ID.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "SyntheticDetectionPolicy" -SyntheticMediaDetection Enabled -SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId "<supported-provider-app-id>" ... Replace `<supported-provider-app-id>` with the Teams App ID of a supported certified detection provider
claims.fix: Keep the call and Teams App ID wording. Append to controls[0].note: 'The feature overview's PowerShell example labels this value as a provider bot application ID, while the cmdlet reference explicitly requires the supported provider Teams App ID, not an arbitrary Entra application ID or bot ID.' The differing example is at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/third-party-synthetic-audio-video-detection-meetings.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy with -SyntheticMediaDetection Disabled turns detection off for that policy regardless of its configured provider.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "SyntheticDetectionPolicy" -SyntheticMediaDetection Disabled ... disables synthetic audio/video detection for meetings organized by users assigned this policy, regardless of the configured detection provider.

claims.where: controls[0].scope and note; Scope: Users and policies; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The detection policy applies to meetings organized by users assigned that policy.
claims.quote: Controls whether synthetic audio/video detection is permitted for meetings organized by users assigned this policy.

claims.claim: Successfully saving the policy does not confirm that the App ID identifies a supported provider.
claims.quote: Successfully saving the policy does not guarantee that the App ID identifies a supported provider or that the detection bot can join meetings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: An incorrect or unsupported App ID can prevent the detection bot from joining eligible meetings.
claims.quote: An incorrect or unsupported App ID can prevent the detection bot from joining eligible meetings.

claims.quote: | Calls.AccessMedia.All | application | The app is a meeting-recording bot

claims.claim: Reality Defender justifies its media permission as real-time audio and video access for authenticity and deepfake analysis.
claims.quote: it needs Graph to join Teams meetings and access the real-time audio and video media in order to run authenticity and deepfake analysis.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Reality Defender's listing is developer self-assessment information whose accuracy Microsoft does not guarantee.
claims.quote: The information on this page is based on a self-assessment report provided by the app developer on the security, compliance, and data handling practices followed by this app. Microsoft makes no guarantees regarding the accuracy of the information.

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents contains details of synthetic media detection events in Teams.
claims.quote: The `SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents` table in the advanced hunting schema contains details about synthetic media (deepfake) detection events in Microsoft Teams in your organization.

claims.claim: The hunting table is populated from Defender for Office 365 records.
claims.quote: This advanced hunting table is populated by records from Microsoft Defender for Office 365.

claims.claim: The table contains data only when an approved detection engine is used.
claims.quote: This table contains data only if you're using an approved detection engine: Microsoft or a third-party engine (GetReal, Pindrop, Reality Defender, or Resemble AI).

claims.claim: Hunting synthetic media detections in Teams is a Microsoft 365 E5 or Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 capability.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5 and Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 extend Teams protection ... Hunting on synthetic media (deepfake) detections in Teams: You can hunt for synthetic media (deepfake) detected in Microsoft Teams using the SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents advanced hunting table.

claims.claim: The hunting table includes detected users' display names.
claims.quote: | `DetectedUserDisplayName` | `string` | Display name of the user flagged as using synthetic media |

claims.claim: The hunting table includes meeting names and identifiers.
claims.quote: `SourceId`: Unique identifier of the source (for example, call ID for meetings or calls ...). `SourceContextName`: Name of the source (for example, the meeting, file, or email name)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Prerequisites; Governance controls
claims.claim: Third-party bots can report detections only when the meeting tenant administrator grants Calls.ReportSyntheticMedia.All as an application permission.
claims.quote: Third-party bots can invoke this action only when the meeting tenant administrator grants the app the `Calls.ReportSyntheticMedia.All` application permission.

claims.claim: In private preview, the organizer can Remove a flagged participant from the alert or roster.
claims.quote: This experience is available only in private preview. ... From the alert or the roster, the organizer can: Remove the flagged participant from the meeting.

claims.claim: In private preview, the organizer can select Mark as not a concern from the alert or roster.
claims.quote: From the alert or the roster, the organizer can: ... Mark as not a concern to dismiss the alert when the organizer has verified the participant.

claims.claim: Teams does not automatically remove participants following a detection.
claims.quote: Teams doesn't remove participants automatically. The organizer decides what action to take.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's publisher-attested listing says hosts can rescan a participant.
claims.quote: Hosts can rescan a participant or end the meeting if manipulation is detected.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's publisher-attested listing says hosts can end the meeting if manipulation is detected.
claims.quote: Hosts can rescan a participant or end the meeting if manipulation is detected.

claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.

claims.claim: Users receive the global meeting policy unless a custom policy is created and assigned.
claims.quote: Users get the global policy unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: An app can be allowed or blocked at Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <value> changes the Teams app's tenant state using a Boolean value.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <String> [-IsBlocked <Boolean>] ... -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app. ... -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference describes -IsBlocked $true as unblocking.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true ... Unblocks Bookings app

claims.claim: App availability, required consent, provider-side activation and meeting policy configuration are separate prerequisites.
claims.quote: A provider appearing in the list doesn't mean that app availability, admin consent, or provider-side activation is complete. ... verify consent, provider-side activation, the organizer's effective policy, and the meeting option.

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetection defaults to Enabled, permitting detection when a configured provider is available.
claims.quote: Enabled: Permits synthetic media detection when a configured detection provider is available. This is the default value. To configure a third-party provider, also set the SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId parameter.

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId defaults to the zero GUID.
The zero GUID default does not select a third-party provider.
claims.quote: It does not select a third-party provider.

claims.claim: The feature page requires the Teams Administrator role or higher to manage the app and meeting policies.
claims.quote: You have the Teams Administrator role (or higher) to manage the app and meeting policies.

claims.claim: The app allow/block control governs the provider app itself, separately from the detection meeting setting.
claims.quote: Step 1: Allow the provider app ... Step 3: Turn on detection in a meeting policy ... App availability and required consent must remain in place for the integration to function.

claims.claim: The App ID parameter reference mentions selecting Microsoft Detection when it is available.
claims.quote: The default value, the zero GUID (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000), selects no provider when Microsoft Detection is unavailable, or Microsoft Detection when it is available.

claims.claim: The medium cost rating reflects the separately licensed provider service rather than an asserted Microsoft fee or meter.
claims.quote: Each provider has its own licensing, service activation, data handling, and support model. Contact the provider directly to purchase or activate its service.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice supplies no General Availability rollout date.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

claims.claim: Disabling SyntheticMediaDetection leaves the configured App ID unchanged.
claims.quote: The SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId value is unchanged.

claims.claim: A detection is the provider's classification rather than proof of manipulation.
claims.quote: Detection (verdict): The provider's assessment that a specific participant's audio, video, or both appear to be synthetic or manipulated. ... Certification doesn't validate the accuracy of a provider's detection models.

claims.claim: Detection providers are independent vendors with their own terms.
claims.quote: Detection provider: An independent software vendor (ISV) whose synthetic media detection solution integrates with Teams ... Evaluate each provider's accuracy claims, privacy statement, and terms against your organization's requirements before you deploy.
